items.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024
items.q: you hear these great songwriters talk about it from Billy Joel to Sting to Carla Bley

ctx.x: If you’re in the midst of arranging a piece do you carry it around with you in your head even when you’re not working on it?

Yeah a hundred percent, yeah. And sometimes to the point of I want it to leave my head and I can’t get it out of my head. And then of course there’s the — you’re committed to it and you’ve done it all and it’s still in your head and you realize oh I wish I had done something different. That’s often part of the equation. So I find it to be a pretty frustrating process to be honest with you Monk, composition in general. And you hear these great songwriters talk about it from Billy Joel to Sting to Carla Bley, you…

I think when you’re writing ‘cause it’s not just going to flow out of you even if you’re really good at it. It’s trial and error. Some things are going to work, some things aren’t and you’re going to want to change stuff. So you’ve got to give yourself some patience.
